notes: The Long Light — a complete story-driven game: you inherit a lighthouse one week before an 88-year tidal phenomenon called the Lending rises, and the whole game builds to the keeper's answer of one question: what is the light for? Five authored chapters and six playable night watches; four interlocking systems (lamp apparatus watch with oil/wick/lens economy, dialogue with trust and consequences, inventory-and-repairs crafting across bell/lens/tower/skiff, day cycle with hours/tides/weather feeding the night); journal/codex, relationship standings, three climax paths and six ending variants, epistolary dawn logs, save/load (autosave + 3 slots, storage guarded), settings (volumes, motion, text speed), pause menu, credits. All art is drawn on canvas (island, lamp room, endings) and all audio is synthesized in code (sea, wind, rain, gulls, bell, foghorn, telegraph, generative music, the Lending's hum, the ticking watch). Accessibility: semantic landmarks, labelled controls, visible focus, full keyboard path (Enter/Space/Esc/J/I/Q/1-5), reduced-motion support, aria-live feeds, colour never carries meaning alone. Verified in a Chromium-based browser via automation: cold start through title, prologue, teaching night, days 1-2, nights 1-2, and a full endgame run (night 5, the rite, the three-path choice, a played-through ending and credits); panels, saves, keyboard shortcuts and responsive layouts at 1600/768/390 px checked; zero console errors observed across all sessions; canvas frame cost measured at 0.16-0.9 ms against a 16.7 ms budget. Limitations: the automation ran in an occluded browser pane, so some screenshot captures showed stale composited frames; scene correctness was therefore additionally verified by direct pixel sampling. All six ending texts were executed and validated; one ending (led_drift) was played live to credits while the other paths share the same verified resolution machinery. English only. Audio starts after the first user gesture per browser policy. Tested over local http; the build uses only relative classic-script loads with no fetch, modules or external assets, so file:// operation is expected but was not directly verified in this environment.
